'''Girsh Blumberg''' is an [[Estonian-American]] physicist working in the [[experimental physics]] fields of [[condensed matter physics]], [[spectroscopy]], [[nano-optics]], and [[plasmon]]ics. 
Blumberg is an elected [[fellow]] of the [[American Physical Society]] (APS),<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2006&unit_id=DCMP&institution=Bell+Laboratories|title= APS Fellow Archive. Citation: For his seminal contributions to elucidating the physics of spin, charge and superconducting correlations in 1D and 2D complex oxide compounds using Raman scattering techniques.|access-date= March 1, 2006|publisher=[[American Physical Society]]}}</ref>
an elected [[Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (FAAAS)
,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aaas.org/fellows/historic|title= Elected AAAS Fellow in 2018. Citation: For distinguished contributions to the field of spectroscopy of electron systems with strong correlations, particularly for Raman spectroscopy of superconductors and quantum magnets.|access-date= November 12, 2018|publisher=[[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]}}</ref>
and a [[Distinguished Professor]] of Physics at [[Rutgers University]].

Girsh Blumberg is best known for his contribution to electronic [[Raman scattering]] studies in [[strongly correlated electrons|strongly correlated electron]] systems,
[[superconductors]] and [[Quantum magnetism|quantum spin systems]].
He has co-authored over 100 publications and is inventor on over 30 patents in the fields of electronic and [[optical devices]], [[spectroscopy]] and nano-[[plasmonics]]. 
He and his collaborators made the first observation of the [[Anthony James Leggett|Leggett]] mode in [[Magnesium diboride|multiband superconductors]],
<ref name=Blumberg2007>{{cite journal| author = Blumberg, G.|title = Observation of Leggett's Collective Mode in a Multiband MgB<sub>2</sub> Superconductor | journal = Physical Review Letters| volume = 99| issue = 22| article-number = 227002|year =2007| doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.99.227002|arxiv = 0710.2803 |last2 = Mialitsin|first2 = A.|last3 = Dennis|first3 = B.S.|last4 = Klein|first4 = M.V.|last5 = Zhigaldo|first5 = N.D.|last6 = Karpinski|first6 = J.|pmid = 18233316 |bibcode = 2007PhRvL..99v7002B|s2cid = 15208599 }}</ref> 
have observed [[Wigner crystal]]lization in strongly interacting quantum spin ladder systems,
<ref name=Blumberg2002>{{cite journal|year=2002|title= Sliding Density-Wave in Sr<sub>14</sub>Cu<sub>24</sub>O<sub>41</sub> Ladder Compounds|journal=[[Science (journal)|Science]]|volume=297 |issue=5581 |pages=547–587|doi=10.1126/science.1070481|pmid= 12142532|arxiv = cond-mat/0207666|last1=Blumberg|first1=G.|last2=Littlewood|first2=P.|last3=Gozar|first3=A.|last4=Dennis|first4=B.S.|last5=Motoyama|first5=N.|last6=Eisaki|first6=H.|last7=Uchida|first7=S.|bibcode= 2002Sci...297..584B|s2cid= 5747865}}</ref>
<ref name=Abbamonte2004>{{cite journal|year=2004|title=Crystallization of charge holes in the spin ladder of Sr<sub>14</sub>Cu<sub>24</sub>O<sub>41</sub> |journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]] |volume=431|pages=1078–1081|doi=10.1038/nature02925|arxiv = cond-mat/0501087|last1=Abbamonte|first1=P.|last2=Blumberg|first2=G.|last3=Rusydi|first3=A.|last4=Gozar|first4=A.|last5=Evans|first5=P.G.|last6=Siegrist|first6=T.|last7=Venema|first7=L.|last8=Eisaki|first8=H.|last9=Isaacs|first9=E.D.|last10=Sawatzky|first10=G.A.|issue=7012 |pmid=15510143 |bibcode=2004Natur.431.1078A|s2cid=4415692 }}</ref>
have explained long-standing puzzle of the "Hidden Order" in [[Uranium ruthenium silicide|URu<sub>2</sub>Si<sub>2</sub>]] [[Heavy fermion material|heavy fermion]] compound,
<ref name=Kung2015>{{cite journal| author = Kung, H.-H.|title = Chirality density wave of the "hidden order" phase in URu<sub>2</sub> Si<sub>2</sub>  |journal=[[Science (journal)|Science]]|volume=347 |issue=6228 |pages=1339–1342|doi=10.1126/science.1259729|pmid= 25678557|arxiv = 1410.6398|last2=Baumbach|first2=R.E.|last3=Bauer|first3=E.D.|last4=Thorsmølle|first4=V.K.|last5=Zhang|first5=W.-L.|last6=Haule|first6=K.|last7=Mydosh|first7=J.A. |last8=Blumberg|first8=G.|year = 2015 |bibcode=2015Sci...347.1339K|s2cid = 30976070 }}</ref>
<ref name=Kung2016>{{cite journal| author = Kung, H.-H.|title = Analogy Between the "Hidden Order" and the Orbital Antiferromagnetism in URu<sub>2-x</sub>Fe<sub>x</sub>Si<sub>2</sub> | journal = Physical Review Letters| volume = 117| issue = 22| article-number = 227601|year =2016| doi =10.1103/PhysRevLett.117.227601|arxiv = 1608.01748|last2=Ran|first2=S.|last3=Kanchanavatee|first3=N.|last4=Krapvin|first4=V.|last5=Lee|first5=A.|last7=Haule|first7=K.|last6=Mydosh|first6=J.A. |last8=Maple|first8=M.B. |last9=Blumberg|first9=G.|pmid = 27925725 |bibcode=2016PhRvL.117v7601K|s2cid = 29468146 }}</ref> 
have made a discovery of the chiral spin waves on the surface of [[topological insulator]]s,
<ref name=Kung2017>{{cite journal| author = Kung, H.-H.|title = Chiral Spin Mode on the Surface of a Topological Insulator | journal = Physical Review Letters| volume = 119| issue = 13| article-number = 136802|year =2017| doi =10.1103/PhysRevLett.119.136802|arxiv = 1706.05776|last2=Maiti|first2=S.|last3=Wang|first3=X.|last4=Cheong|first4=S.-W.|last5=Maslov|first5=D.L.| last6=Blumberg|first6=G.|pmid = 29341673 |bibcode=2017PhRvL.119m6802K|s2cid = 35024953 }}</ref> 
to name a few.

==Biography==
Girsh Blumberg was raised in [[Viljandi]], [[Estonia]] of educator parents, along with his two sisters Riina and Liia.
<ref>{{cite web|url=http://wwx.sakala.ajaleht.ee/191204/esileht/5013861_1.php|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130106144604/http://wwx.sakala.ajaleht.ee/191204/esileht/5013861_1.php|archive-date=January 6, 2013|title=Tartu haridusega USA tipplaboris|work=[[Sakala (newspaper)|Sakala]]|language=Estonian|access-date=December 30, 2012|date=December 18, 2004|first=Tiina |last=Sarv}}</ref>
Blumberg graduated from secondary school in 1976 with gold medal and then, in 1981, with M.Sc. [[Latin honors#Estonia|cum laude]] from [[University of Tartu]].
He completed his Ph.D. in Physics and Mathematics from Physics Institute of the [[Estonian Academy of Sciences]] in 1987.
<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.etis.ee/portaal/isikuCV.aspx?LastNameFirstLetter=B&PersonVID=55576&FromUrl0=isikud.aspx&lang=en|title= Girsh Blumberg|website=Etis.ee|access-date=January 4, 2020}}</ref> 
Starting from 1981 he was first a research, and later a senior research scientist at the [[National Institute of Chemical Physics and Biophysics]] in [[Tallinn]], [[Estonia]].
Between 1992 and 1998 Blumberg was Visiting Research Assistant Professor of the NSF Science and Technology Center for Superconductivity (NSF-STCS) at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]]. 
In 1998 he joined [[Bell Labs]] before joining the faculty at [[Rutgers University]] in 2008.
<ref>{{cite web|url=http://cgisvr.physics.rutgers.edu/cgi-bin/physdb/genpip.pl?Blumberg|title= Girsh Blumberg|publisher= [[Rutgers University]] |access-date=January 4, 2020}}</ref>
